title: 682. Which mountain range forms a natural barrier between Europe and Asia?
hint: It runs through western Russia.
summary: The Ural Mountains are traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia.

title: 683. Which mountain range separates Spain and France?
hint: It stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.
summary: The Pyrenees form the natural border between Spain and France.

title: 684. Which mountain range runs like a backbone through Italy?
hint: Its name comes from the Italian peninsula.
summary: The Apennine Mountains extend along the length of Italy.

title: 685. The Carpathian Mountains are located mainly in which part of Europe?
hint: Countries include Romania, Slovakia and Ukraine.
summary: The Carpathians are located in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: 996. Which Indian classical dance form was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list as part of related traditions?
hint: It is connected with Kerala's traditional theatre.
summary: Koodiyattam is recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage tradition.

title: 997. Which dance form combines martial art movements with performance?
hint: It is a traditional dance-drama from Kerala.
summary: Kathakali includes elements of physical training and martial traditions.

title: 998. Which famous dancer is associated with the revival of Kathakali?
hint: He was a famous Kerala dancer and guru.
summary: Vallathol Narayana Menon contributed greatly to Kathakali revival.

title: 999. Which classical dance form uses the drum instrument called Maddalam?
hint: It is associated with Kerala.
summary: Maddalam is used in Kathakali performances.

title: 622. Which Article gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions?
hint: It follows Article 29.
summary: Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions.

title: 623. Which Article is known as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'?
hint: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar gave this description.
summary: Article 32 is called the Heart and Soul of the Constitution.

title: 624. Which Fundamental Right is called the 'Right to Constitutional Remedies'?
hint: It empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court.
summary: Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

title: 625. Under Article 32, citizens can directly approach:
hint: The highest court in India.
summary: Article 32 allows citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court.

title: 626. Which writ is issued to produce a person who has been illegally detained?
hint: Literally means 'produce the body'.
summary: Habeas Corpus protects personal liberty against unlawful detention.

title: 24. Which river forms the world's largest delta?
summary: The Ganga-Brahmaputra river system forms the Sundarbans Delta.

title: 25. Which Indian state has the highest forest cover in terms of area?
summary: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area among Indian states.

title: 26. Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
summary: Black soil, also known as Regur soil, retains moisture and is ideal for cotton cultivation.

title: 27. Which winds bring rainfall to most parts of India?
summary: The Southwest Monsoon accounts for nearly 75% of India's annual rainfall.

title: 28. Which is the largest coral reef system in the world?
summary: The Great Barrier Reef off Australia's coast is the world's largest coral reef system.

title: 29. Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
summary: The Kosi River frequently changes course and causes devastating floods in Bihar.

title: 30. Which Indian state produces the highest amount of tea?
summary: Assam is India's leading tea-producing state.

title: 531. Which mammal is known as the 'Sea Cow'?
hint: Lives in shallow coastal waters.
summary: Dugong is an endangered marine mammal.

title: 532. Which bird is called the 'flagship species' of Indian grasslands?
hint: State bird of Rajasthan.
summary: Great Indian Bustard is Critically Endangered.

title: 535. Which reptile has the longest snout among crocodilians?
hint: Found in Chambal River.
summary: Gharial is Critically Endangered.

title: 537. Which endangered deer is called Kashmir Stag?
hint: Found in Dachigam.
summary: Hangul is endemic to Kashmir.

title: 550. Which law provides the highest protection to India's endangered wildlife?
hint: Enacted in 1972.
summary: Wildlife (Protection) Act is India's key wildlife law.

title: 30. The capital city of the Kushan Empire was located at which place?
summary: Peshawar, known as Purushapura, was a major capital of the Kushan Empire under Kanishka.

title: 31. Which Harappan site shows evidence of the earliest ploughed field?
summary: Kalibangan in Rajasthan shows the earliest known evidence of a ploughed agricultural field.

title: 32. Chandragupta II adopted which title after his victory over the Saka rulers?
summary: Chandragupta II adopted the title 'Vikramaditya' after defeating the Saka rulers.

title: 33. Which ruler built the Qutub Minar?
summary: Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

title: 34. The Charter Act of 1833 made which provision?
summary: The Charter Act of 1833 centralized Indian administration by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.

title: 35. The 'Sixteen Mahajanapadas' are first mentioned in which ancient text?
summary: The Anguttara Nikaya of Buddhist literature first lists the Sixteen Mahajanapadas.

title: 36. Who built the famous Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur?
summary: Rajaraja Chola I constructed the Brihadeeswara Temple, showcasing Chola architectural brilliance.

title: 569. Which city is situated on the banks of the Yamuna River?
hint: India's capital.
summary: Delhi is located on the Yamuna.

title: 570. Which city is famous for the Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
hint: Located on the Odisha coast.
summary: Konark is famous for its Sun Temple.

title: 571. Which city is known as the 'Tea City of India'?
hint: Located in Assam.
summary: Dibrugarh is India's Tea City.

title: 572. What is the capital of Kerala?
hint: Starts with 'T'.
summary: Thiruvananthapuram is the capital of Kerala.

title: 573. Which city is known as the 'Gateway of South India'?
hint: Major port city of Tamil Nadu.
summary: Chennai is called the Gateway of South India.

title: 718. Which gap separates the Nilgiri Hills from the Anaimalai Hills?
hint: It is an important transport corridor between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
summary: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap separates the Nilgiri and Anaimalai Hills.

title: 719. Which mountain range lies between the Narmada and Tapti rivers?
hint: It is located south of the Narmada River.
summary: The Satpura Range lies between the Narmada and Tapti rivers.

title: 720. Which mountain range lies north of the Narmada River?
hint: It forms the traditional boundary between North and South India.
summary: The Vindhya Range lies north of the Narmada River.

title: 721. Which is the highest peak of the Satpura Range?
hint: It is located in Madhya Pradesh.
summary: Dhupgarh is the highest peak of the Satpura Range.

title: 722. Dhupgarh is located in which famous hill station?
hint: It is the only hill station in Madhya Pradesh.
summary: Dhupgarh is located in Pachmarhi.

title: 723. Which mountain range is also known as the Sahyadri?
hint: It runs parallel to the Arabian Sea coast.
summary: The Western Ghats are also known as the Sahyadris.

title: Which dynasty ruled an important part of northern Tamil Nadu before the rise of the Imperial Cholas?
description: Identify the dynasty associated with Kanchipuram and major developments in South Indian temple architecture.
hint: Their capital was Kanchipuram.
summary: The Pallavas ruled a major part of northern Tamil Nadu and were centered at Kanchipuram.

title: What was the capital of the Pallavas?
description: Identify the principal political and cultural center of the Pallava kingdom.
hint: It is an important historic city in present-day Tamil Nadu.
summary: Kanchipuram was the principal capital of the Pallavas.

title: Which Pallava ruler is regarded as one of the earliest important rulers of the dynasty?
description: Identify the ruler associated with the early consolidation of Pallava power.
hint: His name appears frequently in discussions of early Pallava history.
summary: Simhavishnu was an important early Pallava ruler who expanded Pallava influence southward.

title: Who succeeded Simhavishnu as an important Pallava ruler?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler who was known for his patronage of architecture and literature.
hint: He was the father of Narasimhavarman I.
summary: Mahendravarman I succeeded Simhavishnu and became an important Pallava ruler.

title: 132. Which Tiger Reserve is known as the 'Mini Kaziranga of Assam'?
hint: It has a very high density of wildlife in a comparatively small area.
summary: Orang Tiger Reserve is popularly called the Mini Kaziranga.

title: 133. Which Tiger Reserve is located in Arunachal Pradesh and was declared in 2017?
hint: Its name begins with 'K'.
summary: Kamlang Tiger Reserve became Arunachal Pradesh's second tiger reserve.

title: 134. Which Tiger Reserve forms part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in Tamil Nadu?
hint: It shares boundaries with Bandipur and Wayanad.
summary: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve is a key component of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

title: 135. Which Tiger Reserve is famous as the former stronghold of the forest brigand Veerappan?
hint: Located in Tamil Nadu and acts as an important wildlife corridor.
summary: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve is known for its strategic location between Western and Eastern Ghats.

title: Which Ramsar Site is located in Himachal Pradesh and is a major reservoir?
description: Identify the Ramsar Site formed by the reservoir of a major dam.
hint: It is associated with the Beas River.
summary: Pong Dam Lake is a Ramsar Site in Himachal Pradesh.

title: Which Ramsar Site is a high-altitude wetland in Himachal Pradesh?
description: Identify the high-altitude lake designated as a Ramsar Site.
hint: It is also known as Chandratal.
summary: Chandertal Wetland is a high-altitude Ramsar Site in Himachal Pradesh.

title: Which Ramsar Site is located in Punjab and is associated with the Sutlej-Beas wetland system?
description: Identify the wetland formed at the confluence region of major rivers.
hint: Its name is also the name of a village near the Sutlej.
summary: Harike Wetland is a Ramsar Site in Punjab.

title: Which Ramsar Site is located in Haryana and is a national park?
description: Identify the Ramsar Site famous for migratory birds near Delhi.
hint: It is located in Gurugram district.
summary: Sultanpur National Park is a Ramsar Site in Haryana.

title: 1474. Which religious group received cave donations from Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha?
hint: The group was a contemporary ascetic sect.
summary: The Ajivikas received donations of caves during the Mauryan period, particularly at Barabar and Nagarjuni.

title: 1475. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with the spread of Buddhism beyond India?
hint: He sent Buddhist missions to several regions.
summary: Ashoka played a major role in the spread of Buddhism through missions and royal patronage.

title: 1476. What was the main purpose of Ashoka's edicts?
hint: They communicated the ruler's policies and moral principles.
summary: Ashoka's edicts communicated his Dhamma, administrative instructions, moral principles and messages to his subjects.

title: 1485. What animal appears at the top of the Ashokan Lion Capital at Sarnath?
hint: There are four of them facing different directions.
summary: The Sarnath Lion Capital has four Asiatic lions standing back to back.

title: 1486. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally said to have embraced Jainism toward the end of his life?
hint: He was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
summary: According to Jain traditions, Chandragupta Maurya became associated with Jainism and spent his final years at Shravanabelagola.

title: 689. Which mountain is known as the 'Savage Mountain' because of its difficult climbing conditions?
hint: It is the second-highest peak in the world.
summary: K2 is famously known as the 'Savage Mountain'.

title: 690. Which mountain is popularly known as the 'Killer Mountain' due to its high fatality rate among climbers?
hint: It is located in Pakistan.
summary: Nanga Parbat is popularly known as the 'Killer Mountain'.

title: 691. Which mountain peak is known as 'Sagarmatha' in Nepal?
hint: It is the highest mountain in the world.
summary: Mount Everest is called 'Sagarmatha' in Nepali.
